letter.subject: Please support SafeRX
letter.greeting: Dear Senator and Assembly members of District {district},
letter.body:
I live in your district. Please sponsor and support SafeRX.

SafeRX would require New Jersey pharmacies to give medicine labels, warning stickers, and pharmacist advice in each patient's language.

Many New Jerseyans have limited English. If they can't read their medicine label, they can take the wrong dose. New York and California already protect these patients. New Jersey should too.

Please tell me where you stand on SafeRX.

laws.title: Laws that already work
laws.subtitle: New York and California already protect patients. SafeRX builds on both.

ny.name: New York
ny.who: Chain pharmacies with 8 or more stores in the state
ny.what: Free translated labels, warnings, and written info, plus an interpreter for counseling
ny.languages: Up to 7 per region, each spoken by at least 1% of residents
ny.extra: Pharmacies must post a sign telling patients about this right.

ca.name: California
ca.what: Translated directions for use, on request, on the label or a separate sheet
ca.languages: State translations in Chinese, Farsi, Korean, Russian, Spanish, and Vietnamese
ca.extra: English stays on the label. Pharmacies may add other languages.

laws.takeaway: SafeRX brings both ideas to New Jersey: translated labels and warnings, plus counseling in your language.

preview.disclaimer: Example only. Not medical advice. Real labels need professional medical translation.

label.directions: Take 1 capsule by mouth 3 times a day for 10 days.
warnings: Finish all of this medicine, even if you feel better.
Call your doctor right away if you get a rash or have trouble breathing.
label.counseling: Free advice in your language. Ask your pharmacist.

items.a: A proposed New Jersey bill. Pharmacies would give labels, warnings, and advice in your language. It is not law yet.
Anyone who struggles with English, plus their families and caregivers. Many are seniors and immigrants.

items.q: What do New York and California do?
items.a: New York requires large chain pharmacies to offer free translated labels and interpreters. California requires translated directions on request, and the state provides approved translations. SafeRX builds on both.
They are widely spoken in New Jersey. The Board of Pharmacy can add more later.
Medical translators write and check one shared set. Pharmacies don't translate on their own.
Costs should be low. Pharmacies use free state translations and their current software. The bill would set the timeline.
Sign the petition, send a letter, share this page, and invite your group to join.
